L40: Three isozymes of catechol 1,2-dioxygenase (pyrocatechase) from Pseudomonas arvilla C-1 were separated using DEAE-Toyopearl chromatography. The specific activities of each isozyme were similar to one another. The molecular weights of isozymes 1, 2, and 3 were estimated to be approximately 67,000, 64,000, and 59,000, respectively, from gel filtration.
L41: On sodium dodecyl sulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis, isozymes 1 and 3 gave a single protein band, corresponding to Mr = 32,000 and 30,000, respectively, and isozyme 2 gave two bands corresponding to Mr = 32,000 and 30,000. These results indicated that isozymes 1 and 3 were homodimers, while isozyme 2 was a heterodimer.
L42: The NH2-terminal sequences up to 20 residues of these three isozymes confirmed that isozymes 1, 2, and 3 consisted of beta beta, alpha beta, and alpha alpha, respectively, based on our previous data (Nakai, C., Kagamiyama, H., Saeki, Y., and Nozaki, M. (1979) Arch. Biochem. Biophys. 195, 12-22). Properties of these isozymes such as absorption spectrum, iron content, substrate specificity, and kinetic constants were similar to one another.
L43: Subunit exchange between the different isozymes and dissociation of the isozymes into subunits was not observed under nondenaturing conditions. Available evidence indicates that these isozymes exist naturally in the bacterium and were not due to artifacts caused by purification.

L402: DISCUSSION
L403: 
L404: Catechol 1,2-dioxygenase purified from P. arvilla C-l has
L405: 
L406: been believed to be a homogeneous enzyme consisting of two
L407: 
L408: nonidentical subunits, LY and p (2, 3). However, the purified
L409: 
L410: enzyme was found to be separated further into three active
L411: 
L412: fractions by DEAE-Toyopearl chromatography. From the re-
L413: 
L414: sults of SDS-PAGE, NH,-terminal sequence analysis and
L415: 
L416: molecular weight determination, we assigned the enzymes
L417: from chromatography fractions I, II, and III as isozymes p&
L418: 
L419: a& and (~a, respectively (Figs. l-4).
L420: 
L421: Separation of the enzyme activity by DEAE-Toyopearl
L422: 
L423: chromatography was not due to artificial modifications of the
L424: 
L425: enzyme during the purification, because the crude extract of
L426: 
L427: P. arvilla C-l also showed three activity peaks on the chro-
L428: 
L429: matogram similar to those of the purified enzyme (Figs. 1 and
L430: 
L431: 9). These isozymes were also separated by HPLC using a
L432: TSKgel DEAE-5PW column. (Y@ and the mixture of &3 and
L433: 
L434: OI(Y showed only the original peaks by HPLC, respectively,
L435: 
L436: when they were kept at 0 “C for 2-4 weeks (Fig. 8), indicating
L437: 
L438: that interchange of the subunits did not occur under these
L439: 
L440: conditions. Taking these results together, we conclude that
L441: 
L442: these three isozymes exist naturally in the bacterium.

L513: Three isozymes of catechol 1,2-dioxygenase are formed by
L514:

L518: 
L519: genes since their primary structures are different from each
L520: 
L521: other. To our knowledge, these isozymes are the first case of
L522: this type among catechol dioxygenases. Several isozymes
L523: 
L524: formed by combinations of nonidentical subunits are well
L525: 
L526: known in mammals. Five types of lactate dehydrogenase (EC
